author: Bobby Grayson
description: General lesson for the method: a bounded check over a state predicate cannot express conservation (what is held plus what is in flight is determined by what arrived). When a property is about a step rather than a state, prove it; do not weaken it into a state predicate and then describe it as if it were the strong version. Also fixed: check.sh was suppressing translator stderr for log_store.ex, hiding a real registered-name warning.
title: Round 8 verifier found two of four bounded checks nearly vacuous, proven empirically with its own mutants: LogStore's check constrained the counter only, so a behaviour that never appended to the buffer passed; LogsLive's check only asked that the seed stay a prefix, so a behaviour dropping every message passed, as did one appending twice. Fixed: LogStore now checks count = buffer length AND length <= cap (both mutants caught, 7 and 3 configurations); LogsLive's missing property is a STEP property the state-predicate explorer cannot express, so it is proven instead (stepConserves, not_dropping, not_duplicating). README claims corrected to match
